  - [HIGH] Log injection via unescaped geometry form values in widget (LogicAgent)

findings.title: Log injection via unescaped geometry form values in widget
findings.description: Log injection vulnerability: The user-controlled 'value' variable is interpolated directly into the log message. An attacker can supply a value containing newlines, carriage returns, or ANSI escape sequences (e.g., 'line\nbreak' or 'ESC[31mred') to forge log entries or obscure legitimate log data in terminal-based or stream-based log aggregation systems.
findings.suggestion: Sanitize or escape the 'value' variable before logging, ensuring control characters (especially \n, \r, \x1b) are stripped or escaped so that the log record remains single-line and non-manipulable. Consider using repr(value) or explicit string escaping prior to passing it to logger.error.

findings.title: Potential Log Injection via Unsanitized Geometry Input in Error Logging
findings.description: User-supplied geometry input is trimmed of control characters before logging, but the trimmed value itself may still contain log-injection payloads (e.g., newlines or ANSI escape sequences) that have not been sanitized. The log_message function likely performs its own escaping, but if it does not, or if this code path is bypassed, the raw value can be injected into logs. The diff also removes the test that validated this escaping behavior, removing the safety net. This is a low-severity information disclosure/log manipulation issue.
findings.suggestion: Ensure that the value passed to logger.error is explicitly escaped using a safe string formatting function or a dedicated log-sanitization utility before it reaches the logging layer. Restore or update the test case to verify that control characters and ANSI sequences are neutralized in the final log output.

findings.title: Log Injection Vulnerability Reintroduced by Direct Logging of Raw Input
findings.description: The direct logger.error call now passes the raw, untrimmed value into the log message. While the logging module in Python 3 handles basic string substitution safely, if the underlying logging handler or backend (e.g., a file handler, syslog, or a custom handler) does not sanitize control characters or escape sequences, an attacker can inject newlines or ANSI codes into the log file. This reverts a previous hardening that trimmed and explicitly escaped the value. The risk is that log integrity is compromised, potentially hiding malicious entries or spoofing log lines.
findings.suggestion: Sanitize the `value` variable by removing or escaping control characters (specifically \n, \r, \t, and ANSI escape sequences like \x1b) before passing it to logger.error. For example, use `value.replace('\n', '\\n').replace('\x1b', '\\x1b')` or a dedicated sanitization helper. Alternatively, use a logging formatter that automatically escapes these characters.
